tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Kavvanot when Washing One's Body Before Shabbes, by Eyal Raviv

tei:div.tei:head: Kavvanot when Washing One's Body Before Shabbes, by Eyal Raviv

tei:l.tei:hi: Washing from head down, as you wash each part in the manner you wish, think about what the parts of your body may physically or spiritually represent.

tei:div.tei:head: head
tei:div.tei:p: Let me think of others without judgment, of situations with thoughts of kindness for all involved and not of problems, but possibilities...

tei:div.tei:head: face: ears, eyes, mouth
tei:div.tei:p: Let me not hear and see only what I want or wish, but to consider all sides of a situation; let me not speak words of slander, malice or carelessness but utter those that bring clarity, comfort or joy...

tei:div.tei:head: chest
tei:div.tei:p: Let me act with the intent of my soul, to be aware of the possibilities in every heartbeat within me and to remember to feel the emotions of the actions I take...

tei:div.tei:head: arms/hands
tei:div.tei:p: Let my hands create and work to bring about the change for good that is in my heart. Let them hug more than hit and create more than destroy...

tei:div.tei:head: stomach and genital areas
tei:div.tei:p: Let me not be driven solely by inner desires and selfish needs; let me consider goals that are more meaningful to me than temporary satisfactions...

tei:div.tei:head: legs and feet
tei:div.tei:p: Let me move and act for the change I wish to see in this world for as long as my legs will carry me...

tei:l.tei:hi: Let the words of your heart and your true intentions of a perfect you continue through the space under the water and carry you into Shabbat.
